Hello! 👋

@vvo @bobylito @LukyVj 

I used this icon because it's something I'm used to seeing around to web for both 'copy to clipboard' and 'duplicate' 

I usually go to thenounproject to make sure is not something subjective: 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26247132/27534162-5792ca38-5a66-11e7-9713-4e1b0c8163f4.png)

In my opinion, if there's an icon for a simple action like this one it's better to use that than text as it's easier to process quickly and it separates better from the written word which in this case is abundant. However, I can't speak for a user of documentation, if you guys think it's still better to go with text I don't think it's a 'design breaker' 🤷‍♀️

Indeed as a dev it was not obvious what this button does, it looks very similar to open link in a new window (something you generally don't want to happen): 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/123822/27535611-edfad61e-5a6b-11e7-8a4c-0bb8c6504cfa.png), from https://thenounproject.com/search/?q=popup%20window&i=539930

We could either have a nice text button with "copy" (no need for copy to clipboard) button, much like we have "edit on github". If we want to go for an icon, that one is more often seen in documentations: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/123822/27535648-1347051e-5a6c-11e7-8518-e03bf1590691.png), from https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Octicons-clippy.svg. It's the copy button that was on GitHub for years and thus is something immediately recognisable by all developers.

So, I arrive a bit after the war, but I don't see the problem of having an icon instead of text. 
Plus, we do it on the dashboard for our customers, most of them are regular profiles I guess ( not so dev in some cases ) and we still show them this icon. 

I'm not strongly for having an icon instead of text, but since we do it on algolia.com, I don't see why it would be a problem on a community website. 

![](https://puu.sh/wuE1O/3dff43ecd9.png)

So if I sum up:
 - this icon can be confusing (@vvo didn't get the meaning of this icon)
 - icons are better, especially for such icons. But needs to be easily recognizable
 - if something is more universal than the other, let's choose the more universal

@auareyoualgolia do you have another proposal of icon that would be more universal?
The one on algolia.com works better to me. We just have to settle on one common icon for our websites (thus either algolia.com one or the clippy.svg one that is very common)

I agree with you @vvo, it's true that the one on the design is more for "open in a new page" but in the end, I think we can find a better one (reusing the one of the dashboard?) and it will bring design consistency across our different pages. 

And as Sebastien says, good design = consistent design = trust
I think reusing the one from the dashboard would make sense too. I thought it a slightly different use but it is true it's much more clear
